planting.note: Direct sow or set transplants after soil has warmed well into the 70s; Alvaro is one of the earliest-ripening Charentais types, a useful trait where summers are short.

directions: Alvaro is a French-type Charentais hybrid noted for ripening earlier than most other Charentais melons, producing compact, deeply sutured round fruit without netting on a smooth, yellowish-tan rind lightly striped in green. The thick orange flesh is dense and aromatic, filling the air with the intense perfume typical of Charentais types when fully ripe. Because Charentais melons slip from the vine only at peak ripeness, check daily as fruit nears maturity and watch for a slight crack or softening at the stem end. Give it full sun and warm, fertile, well-drained soil, keeping moisture steady through fruit set and tapering off as the small melons ripen to concentrate sugars.
sources: Territorial Seed Company — Alvaro Melon Seed

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into warm soil; Savor has good resistance to Fusarium wilt and intermediate resistance to powdery mildew, helping fruit finish well in humid climates.

directions: Savor is a mid-to-late French Charentais hybrid prized by market growers for combining classic Charentais eating quality with a notably long shelf life of up to two weeks after harvest. The small, slightly flattened, 1.5-2 pound fruit has faintly ribbed, smooth gray-green skin enclosing deep orange, intensely aromatic flesh. Because Charentais types only slip cleanly from the vine when fully ripe, inspect plants daily near the expected harvest window and look for a slight crack or softening at the stem end. Its disease resistance and extended keeping quality make it a reliable choice for roadside stands and farmers markets as well as home gardens.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds — Savor (F1) Melon Seed
Osborne Seed Company — Savor F1 Melon Seeds

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; D'Artagnan is an extra-early Charentais, ripening about a week ahead of most other Charentais hybrids, which suits shorter growing seasons.

directions: D'Artagnan is an extra-early French Charentais hybrid bred to bring true Charentais eating quality to gardeners with shorter summers than the classic Charentais growing region. The round to slightly oval, two-pound fruit has green-sutured skin with moderate netting and rich, dark orange flesh carrying the traditional sweet, aromatic Charentais flavor. Harvest by cutting from the vine when the skin turns green with a yellowish tinge rather than waiting for a full slip. Resistance to Fusarium wilt and powdery mildew helps the vines stay productive through the short harvest window typical of this earliest-maturing Charentais type.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds — D'Artagnan (F1) Melon Seed

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into warm soil; Anna's Charentais was bred specifically for longer post-harvest storage than most French Charentais types.

directions: Anna's Charentais is a French-type melon hybrid bred for longer shelf life than typical Charentais varieties while keeping the classic small size and mild aromatic sweetness of the type. The compact 2-3 pound fruit has the traditional smooth, lightly ribbed Charentais look and stores six days or more at room temperature, considerably longer than most Charentais melons, which makes it well suited to fresh-market sales as well as the home garden. Harvest at forced slip or cut from the vine as the skin begins turning yellow. Resistance to Fusarium wilt and intermediate tolerance of powdery mildew help keep vines productive through harvest.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds — Anna's Charentais (F1) Melon Seed
Osborne Seed Company — Anna's Charentais F1 Melon Seeds

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; Griselet is a modern hybrid bred to recreate the heirloom Petit Gris de Rennes with improved disease resistance.

directions: Griselet is a Charentais hybrid bred as a disease-resistant counterpart to the French heirloom Petit Gris de Rennes, reproducing its old-fashioned appearance and flavor on vigorous, healthier vines. The fruit has a distinctive greenish-yellow rind marked with green sutures and an intoxicating perfume as it ripens. Inside, the flesh is succulent, sweet, and creamy, with a flavor many describe as touched with exotic spice notes beyond typical Charentais sweetness. Harvest by cutting from the vine once the skin yellows and the rind gives slightly under gentle pressure, and grow in full sun with warm, fertile, well-drained soil for the best flavor concentration.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds — Griselet (F1) Charentais Melon Seed

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into warm soil; Arava is noted for good powdery mildew tolerance and reliable performance across a range of climates, including cooler-than-ideal summers.

directions: Arava is a widely grown Galia-type melon hybrid originating from Israeli breeding programs, valued for uniform, round fruit up to about four pounds with a thin but tough, raised corky netting over the rind. The flesh is pale green, thick, smooth, and fine-grained, with the intensely perfumed sweetness characteristic of Galia melons rather than the heavier musk of American cantaloupe. Harvest at full slip, when the fruit separates cleanly from the vine with light pressure and the characteristic Galia fragrance is strong at the blossom end. Good resistance to powdery mildew helps vines stay productive over a long harvest season in full sun and warm, well-drained soil.
sources: Fedco Seeds — Arava Organic Galia-Type Melon
Johnny's Selected Seeds — Organic Arava (F1) Melon Seed

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; Diplomat is an early Galia type with powdery mildew resistance, ripening a concentrated early set of fruit.

directions: Diplomat is an early Galia-type melon hybrid that produces a concentrated set of five to six pound fruit on healthy, vigorous vines with good resistance to powdery mildew. The rind has sparse netting, and the thick green flesh has a small seed cavity and an exceptionally sweet, aromatic eating quality typical of Galia types. Harvest at full slip, when the skin turns yellow and the fruit releases cleanly from the vine with light pressure. Grow in full sun with warm, fertile, well-drained soil and even moisture through fruit set, tapering off as the melons approach ripeness to concentrate their sugars.
sources: Johnny's Selected Seeds — Diplomat (F1) Galia Melon Seed
William Dam Seeds — Diplomat Hybrid Melon
